data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2021 were GBP 180.512m. Using the Syndicate's gross claims development table, prior-year development (years up to and including 2019) produced a net adverse movement of approximately GBP 6.325m (c. 3.5% of opening reserves), i.e. a strengthening of reserves. The adverse movement was driven primarily by deterioration in the 2019 underwriting year (notably contingency/COVID-19 related exposures) and development on prior property catastrophe/typhoon losses, with currency considerations noted for Japanese Yen-denominated losses.
raw_causal_phrases: This year, which has again been dominated by COVID-19, saw more catastrophe activity with perils such as floods, freezes and inland windstorms again causing headlines.

This was, on the whole, due to some deterioration in the Contingency account's COVID-19 claims, as changing lockdown restrictions caused some rescheduled events to be rescheduled again or even finally cancelled where further rescheduling was no longer practical.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (claims incurred cumulative by underwriting year) on page 44 because the report does not present an explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision' figure. The triangle values are in GBP '000. No explicit verbatim sentence quantifying gross prior year reserve movement was found; exact_reserve_text left blank. RITC and closed-year movements exist in the report (2019 RITC close) but the triangle appears not to be obviously distorted by RITC entries for the years used. Confidence in the PYD calculation is set to 0.8 (calculated from triangle).
